# inlavanilla

> INLA-style skew-normal marginals for any log-posterior.

If you can write down the log-likelihood plus the log-prior,
[inlavanilla](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/) gives you approximate
Bayesian inference for the parameters of your model: posterior marginals
and draws, the marginal likelihood, and leave-one-out cross-validation.
There is no sampler and no tuning, and small models take milliseconds.
It runs the approximation pipeline of
[INLAvaan](https://inlavaan.haziqj.ml/) with nothing model-specific:

1.  a **Laplace approximation** at the posterior mode, with the Laplace
    estimate of the log marginal likelihood;
2.  a **VB mean correction** that recentres the Gaussian at a better
    estimate of the posterior mean, in one Newton step by default;
3.  **skew-normal marginals**, one per parameter, fitted to scans of the
    log-posterior;
4.  **Gaussian copula draws** for any function of the parameters.

Stages 2 and 3 are optional and independent: `vb_correction = "none"`
skips the VB correction, and `marginals = "gaussian"` keeps the Gaussian
marginals instead of scanning for skew-normal ones. With both, you get
the Laplace approximation alone.

Give [`loo()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) or
[`waic()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) the
log-likelihood as one term per observation, and they estimate the
model’s predictive accuracy from the fit alone, with no refits and no
draws.

The package is pure R and small. Its only dependency outside base R is
[cli](https://cli.r-lib.org/).

## Installation

You can install the development version of inlavanilla from
[GitHub](https://github.com/haziqj/inlavanilla) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("haziqj/inlavanilla")
```

## Example

A trial records 3 responders out of 20 patients. With a uniform prior on
the response rate \\p\\, the posterior is \\\text{Beta}(4, 18)\\:
skewed, and bounded at zero.

[`inla_vanilla()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/inla_vanilla.md)
works best on an unconstrained scale, so we write the log-posterior in
terms of \\\vartheta = \text{logit}(p)\\. The prior is stated for \\p\\,
so it carries the Jacobian \\dp / d\vartheta = p(1 - p)\\. The names of
`init` name the parameters, and calling this one `logit_p` says which
scale it is on:

``` r

library(inlavanilla)

y <- 3
n <- 20

logpost <- function(theta) {
  p <- plogis(theta[["logit_p"]])
  dbinom(y, n, p, log = TRUE) +
    dbeta(p, 1, 1, log = TRUE) + # prior on p ...
    log(p) + log1p(-p) # ... and the Jacobian
}

fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, init = c(logit_p = 0))
#> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 6 iterations [3ms]
#> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.17σ [32ms]
#> ✔ Fitted 1 skew-normal marginal [4ms]
fit
#> ── INLAvanilla v26.11.25 ────────────────────── Skew-normal + one-step VB ──
#> 
#> Log marginal likelihood: -3.05 · Converged in 6 iterations (67ms)
#> 
#>        Mean      SD    2.5%     50%   97.5%    Mode
#> 1 p  0.1819  0.0804  0.0549  0.1723  0.3632  0.1510
#> 
#> ℹ Natural scale: p = plogis(logit_p).
```

Due to the name given to the `init` vector, `inlavanilla` recognises
that the fit is made on the logit scale and reports back on the natural
scale \\p\\. Only the reporting changes: `logpost` still receives
`logit_p`, and `transform = FALSE` turns the renaming off. See the
[natural-scale
summaries](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/natural-scale.html)
vignettes for details.

The summary matches the exact posterior:

``` r

rbind(
  inlavanilla = fit$summary["p", c("2.5%", "50%", "97.5%")],
  exact = qbeta(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), 4, 18)
)
#>                   2.5%       50%    97.5%
#> inlavanilla 0.05491963 0.1722897 0.363167
#> exact       0.05446357 0.1720895 0.363424
```

[`sampling()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/sampling.md)
draws from the approximate posterior. Here, they are seen to have the
skew of the exact posterior:

``` r

set.seed(1)
p <- sampling(fit, nsamp = 1e5)[, "p"]
hist(p, breaks = 80, freq = FALSE, border = NA, col = "#F5D0BE",
     main = NULL, xlab = "Response rate p", ylab = NULL, yaxt = "n")
curve(dbeta(x, 4, 18), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "#C2410C")
```

![Histogram of draws of p, skewed to the right, with the exact Beta(4,
18) density overlaid and matching
it.](reference/figures/README-density-1.png)

`summary(fit)` adds diagnostics for each stage of the approximation, and
`plot(fit)` draws the marginals. The [Get
started](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/inlavanilla.html)
vignette works through a multi-parameter example: it checks the
approximation against the exact posterior, and covers gradients, derived
quantities and model comparison.

## References

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026a). *Approximate Bayesian inference for
structural equation models using integrated nested Laplace
approximations* (arXiv:2603.25690 \[stat.ME\]). arXiv.
<https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690>

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026b). *Implementation and workflows for
INLA-based approximate Bayesian structural equation modelling*
(arXiv:2604.00671 \[stat.CO\]). arXiv.
<https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.00671>

# Package index

## All functions

- [`coef(`*`<inla_vanilla>`*`)`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/coef.inla_vanilla.md)
  : Posterior means of an INLAvanilla fit
- [`diagnostics()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnostics of an INLAvanilla fit
- [`inla_vanilla()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/inla_vanilla.md)
  : INLA-style posterior approximation for any log-posterior
- [`loo()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md)
  [`waic()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) :
  Leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC for an INLAvanilla fit
- [`plot(`*`<inla_vanilla>`*`)`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/plot.inla_vanilla.md)
  : Plot an INLAvanilla fit
- [`rtmb_latent()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/rtmb_latent.md)
  : Draw latent variables from an RTMB object
- [`sampling()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/sampling.md) :
  Draw from an approximate posterior
- [`summary(`*`<inla_vanilla>`*`)`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/summary.inla_vanilla.md)
  : Summarise an INLAvanilla fit
- [`timing()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/timing.md) : Time
  taken by each stage of an INLAvanilla fit
- [`use_vanilla()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/use_vanilla.md)
  : Copy the engine of inlavanilla into a package
- [`use_vanilla_ci()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/use_vanilla_ci.md)
  : Check the engine copy on GitHub Actions
- [`use_vanilla_test()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/use_vanilla_test.md)
  : Add a test that checks the engine copy
- [`vanilla_control()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/vanilla_control.md)
  : Tuning of an INLAvanilla fit
- [`vanilla_status()`](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/vanilla_status.md)
  : Check a copy of the engine of inlavanilla

# Articles

### Get started

- [Get started with
  inlavanilla](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/inlavanilla.md):

### Examples

- [Multilevel
  models](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/multilevel.md):

  A linear mixed model with the random effects integrated out and drawn
  back afterwards, checked against brms.

- [Cognitive diagnostic
  models](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/cdm.md):

  A DINA model for binary items, with the latent classes summed out,
  checked against Stan.

- [Correlation
  matrices](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/correlation.md):

  A multivariate normal with an LKJ prior on its correlation matrix,
  written in terms of canonical partial correlations, checked against
  Stan.

- [Binary factor
  analysis](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/binary-cfa.md):

  A one-factor model for binary items, with the factor integrated out by
  Gauss-Hermite quadrature inside the log-posterior.

- [Diagnostic tests without a gold
  standard](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/diagnostic-tests.md):

  Three latent class models for five schistosomiasis tests in Ghana,
  with the infection status summed out and a random effect integrated by
  quadrature.

### Articles

- [Natural-scale
  summaries](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/natural-scale.md):

- [Diagnostics](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/diagnostics.md):

- [Model comparison with LOO and
  WAIC](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/model-comparison.md):

- [Latent variables](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/latents.md):

  Random effects, class memberships and other latent variables are
  integrated out of the log-posterior. Four ways to draw them back after
  the fit.

- [Speeding up with
  Rcpp](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/rcpp.md):

  A structural equation model with 39 parameters, its log-posterior
  written first in R and then in C++ with Rcpp and RcppEigen, with an
  analytic gradient.

- [Gradients and Hessians with
  RTMB](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/rtmb.md):

  The structural equation model of the Rcpp article written for RTMB,
  which differentiates R code automatically to give the gradient and the
  Hessian, and compared with R and C++ for speed and accuracy.

### For package developers

- [Using the engine in your own
  package](https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/engine.md):
